SF Startup Challenge Hackathon


Date: October 20, 2026 · AWS Builder Loft | Theme: Build an
AI-Native Startup Run by a Team of Agents, Using Band Desktop
and Cognee

The next startup won't be one founder and one chatbot. It will be one founder leading a team of
AI agents: a planner, builders, a reviewer, and a security lead. They share one plan, hand work
to each other, remember what they learned yesterday, and ask the human only when a real
decision is needed.


The SF Startup Challenge asks you to build that kind of company. Use Band Desktop so your
agents work as a coordinated team, and Cognee so they have lasting memory. Then ship a real
product that solves a real startup problem. Bonus points if your product can charge for itself
with Flexprice, and if your agents ship secure code with Snyk.


Core Challenge

Design and build an agentic product (or an agent-powered startup workflow) that:


    ●​ Band Desktop: Runs your agents as one collaborative team in a shared room. They
      work from one plan, claim and finish work items, @mention each other to pass context,
      and bring decisions to the human in one place.
    ●​ Cognee: Gives your agents an AI memory that lasts across sessions, restarts, and
       agents. Your team remembers customers, decisions, code context, and lessons learned
       instead of starting from zero every time.
    ●​  Flexprice (bonus): Meters usage and bills for it with usage-based, credit-based, or
       hybrid pricing, so your startup has a real business model from day one.
    ●​ Snyk (bonus): Scans the code, dependencies, and containers your agents produce, so
      a security check is built into how your agent team ships.

Mandatory Requirements


1. Band Desktop integration (new desktop features)

Your project must use Band Desktop, BAND's new desktop app for coordinating coding agents,
as the coordination layer for your agent team. At minimum:


    ●​ Shared room: Two or more agents work together in one Band room. Using agents from
        different harnesses or frameworks (for example Claude Code with Codex, Copilot,
      OpenCode, or a LangGraph/CrewAI agent) scores higher.
    ●​ One plan, one board: A lead or architect agent writes the plan in the room. Agents claim
      work items and move them from To-do to Done.
    ●​  Agent-to-agent handoffs: Agents @mention each other and pass context directly, with
      no human copy-pasting between them.
    ●​ Human in the loop: At least one real decision or approval (for example running a
      command, editing a file, or a product choice) goes to the human through Band instead
       of being hard-coded.
    ●​  Visibility: Your demo must show Band Desktop's views of the work: rooms, the work
       board, and per-agent sessions, tokens, and estimated cost.


2. Cognee integration (AI memory)

Your agents must use Cognee Open Source as working memory, not as a static document
dump. At minimum:


    ●​ Agents write to memory during the work (for example decisions, customer insights,
      code context, or review findings).
    ●​ Agents recall from memory to change what they do next, and you must show this
       across a session restart or between two different agents.
    ●​  Using improve or forget, or connecting Cognee to a graph backend such as Neo4j,
       earns extra credit within this criterion.


3. Deep integration

Band Desktop and Cognee must be essential to the product. If you can remove either one and
the demo still works the same way, it's bolted on. Integrations that feel like afterthoughts are
grounds for disqualification.

Bonus Integrations (Extra Marks)


Flexprice: Usage-based billing

Use Flexprice to meter real usage events from your product or agents (API calls, tokens, tasks
completed, reports generated) and turn them into a pricing model: usage-based, credits and
top-ups, tiered, or hybrid. Top marks go to projects where metering drives the product, for
example credits that gate features, or agent costs from Band passed through to customer
billing.


Snyk: Secure by default

Use Snyk (CLI, Snyk Code, Snyk Open Source, or Snyk Container) to scan what your agents
build. Top marks go to projects where security is a team member, for example a
security-reviewer agent in the Band room that runs Snyk scans, posts findings, blocks a work
item until it's fixed, and stores recurring issues in Cognee so the team stops repeating them.


Technology Primers

    ●​ Band Desktop (Mission control for agent teams): BAND is interaction infrastructure
        that lets AI agents and humans collaborate in shared rooms, whatever framework each
       agent runs on. Band Desktop (with the jam CLI) is the new desktop app that brings your
        local coding agents into one workspace. It includes shared rooms, a plan and work-item
       board, a Human in the loop column, predefined teams like Feature crew or Bug squad,
         filterable activity trails, approvals before commands or file edits, and sessions, tokens,
      and cost per agent. Your agents keep running on your machine in your own harness;
     BAND carries the messages between them.
    ●​ Cognee (AI memory for agents): Cognee turns conversations, documents, and context
        into a knowledge-graph "AI brain" that agents, apps, and users can query across
       sessions. Add data, cognify it into memory, and search it from any agent. For this
       hackathon, use Cognee Open Source.
    ●​  Flexprice (Open-source usage-based billing - bonus): Flexprice is an open-source,
        developer-first platform for metering, billing, and feature access. Send usage events,
      and it handles aggregation, credits, entitlements, and invoicing for usage-based,
       seat-based, or hybrid pricing. Use the cloud version or self-host it.
    ●​ Snyk (Developer security - bonus): Snyk finds and helps fix vulnerabilities in your
       code, open-source dependencies, containers, and infrastructure-as-code. It runs from
       the CLI, your IDE, or CI.

  Judging Criteria

          ●​ Band Desktop integration (25%): Real multi-agent collaboration, plan and board,
             handoffs, human-in-the-loop.

●​ Cognee integration (25%): Memory that changes agent behavior across sessions and
       agents.
    ●​  Startup viability (20%): Real problem, clear user, believable business.
    ●​  Technical execution and demo quality (20%)
    ●​  Innovation and creativity (10%)
    ●​  Flexprice integration (Bonus - up to +10%)
    ●​ Snyk integration (Bonus - up to +10%)

Submission & Deliverables


What to submit:

    ●​ Working prototype: Live or local demo.
    ●​ Source code: Repository link.
    ●​ Demo video (required, 2–3 min): Must show Band Desktop in action (the room, the
      work board moving, a human decision, and the cost view) and a Cognee memory recall
       changing what an agent does.
    ●​  Project description: The problem, your agent team (roles, harnesses, and how they
      hand off), how you use Cognee memory, and whether you used Flexprice or Snyk and
       how.
    ●​  Pitch deck: Optional.

Setup Checklist - Hacker Guide

    ●​ Band Desktop: Download it from band.ai/download, sign in at app.band.ai, and
        follow the setup guide at docs.band.ai/jam (CLI: brew install
      thenvoi/tap/jam). Connect your first two agents to a room before you start building.
       (https://www.band.ai/hacker-guide)
    ●​ Cognee: Install Cognee Open Source from github.com/topoteretes/cognee and
       configure your LLM and storage (optionally Neo4j as the graph store). Sketch which
      memories your agents will write and read.
    ●​  Flexprice (bonus): Sign up or self-host (docs.flexprice.io), define your meters and
        plan, and send a test usage event.
    ●​ Snyk (bonus): Create a free account at snyk.io, install the Snyk CLI, run snyk auth,
       then snyk test / snyk code test on your repo.



What to fill in or check before publishing:

    ●​ The placeholders for deadline, submission link, and support channel.

●​ Whether sponsors are giving promo codes or credits (like HackwithBay's Butterbase
    code).
●​ The judging weights, if sponsors have their own expectations.
●​ The Band Desktop features I named come from BAND's own product page: agents
    claim work items and move them from To-do to Done, agents can ask a person to
   approve before they run a command or edit a file, right in the room, and the app shows
    sessions, tokens, and estimated cost for every agent and every room. It's worth
    confirming with the BAND team that they want the demo to show these specific
    features.
●​  Older references to "Jam Desktop" now appear as BAND Desktop. The hacker guide
   describes Jam Desktop as the app you download, and the jam CLI as the command-line
    client it installs and keeps up to date.
